context.why: Stories 1 and 2 are accepted. fairdm/core/editing.py holds RecordEditingPage (verdict, may_be_used_by, dispatch, get_object, record_name), EditDetails, EditDescriptions, EditKeyDates, EditIdentifiers and manage_menu, registered on Project, Dataset, Sample and Measurement with menu=False. <c-actions.manage> draws the menu on all four overviews. tests/test_core/test_editing.py holds the tests and fixtures for all of it. This story adds the delete page on all four record types, so a sample and a measurement can be deleted through the portal for the first time, and removes the Delete additional views on the project and dataset overviews with what only they used.
prior_decisions: decisions.md planning decisions D8 to D17: read them, they describe the module as it stands. D13 says the Manage menu draws no divider and no flag for the delete entry yet: this story builds both (an entry flag marking delete, a divider before it in <c-actions.manage>), and removes the delete items the project and dataset templates pass through the component's slot.

access = 'delete' on DeleteRecord. The permission table is already in RecordEditingPage.PERMISSIONS. Deleting any of the four record types needs the manage level; an edit-level person gets 403 and sees the editing entries without the delete entry.

Build on FairDMDeleteView and django-mvp's delete_view.html (.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mvp/views/edit.py MVPDeleteView, around lines 431-700). Read how the existing project and dataset Delete views use it (fairdm/core/project/plugins.py, fairdm/core/dataset/plugins.py) before removing them: require_confirmation, get_confirmation_value, is_protected, protected_objects, setting form to None when protected, and the dataset's related_objects_summary by concrete sample and measurement type.
Confirmation value is the record's name, or its portal ID (uuid) when it has no name. Use record_name for how a measurement is named on the page.

What goes with it: a project and a dataset show counts by record type from one method on the page (move the dataset's existing summary there and make it serve a project too). A sample and a measurement use django-mvp's related-objects preview.

Design review, security: a sample's delete page names only the measurements in Measurement.objects.visible_to(request.user), by name or portal ID, and gives a count for the rest, because a measurement can sit in a dataset the viewer holds no level on. Do not print str(measurement) for a measurement the viewer may not see.

Protection on POST: django-mvp's post() re-collects and refuses a restricted or protected record itself, so the sample case needs no code. PublicDatasetsProtect is raised from a pre_delete signal it does not see, so form_valid catches that one and draws the page again in its protected state, as the existing project Delete view does. Test both.

Landing: a sample or a measurement lands on its dataset's own page, or on the dataset list (dataset-list) when the person may not open that dataset. Read the dataset before deleting. A dataset lands on dataset-list and a project on project-list. Each sets a success message. The Back control leads to the record's own page.

Remove CRUDDirectoryMixin, the remaining crud_views entries and show_delete_action from the project and dataset overviews, and DeletePlugin from fairdm/core/plugins.py. Check nothing else reads `directory` in the overview templates before removing the mixin.

tests/test_contrib/test_contributors/test_plugins/test_shared.py has a refusal helper that still expects 404 from the old deletion page for a viewer who may see a private record; with the shared page that answer is 403.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given the test classes tasks.md T007 lists, when they are run before T008, then they fail because the shared delete page does not exist.

Given a project, a dataset, a demo sample type and a demo measurement type, when someone at each level requests, confirms and is refused the delete page, then every outcome in tasks.md T007 holds and the old delete pages and DeletePlugin are gone.
Given the documentation, when it is read, then record-editing-pages.md covers the delete page and the user guide pages for deleting a project and a dataset describe the shared page.
